items.title: De novo biosynthesis of meroterpenoid grifolic acid in Yarrowia lipolytica
items.summary: Grifolic acid, a potent bioactive meroterpenoid derived from fungi, shows great antitumor and antimicrobial properties. Nevertheless, the difficulty of large-scale chemical production and its minimal presence in natural environments hinder its path toward clinical translation. We developed a de novo grifolic acid biosynthetic route by leveraging the robust metabolic capabilities of the oleaginous yeast Yarrowia lipolytica . By improving the precursor malonyl-CoA supply through ACC1 overexpression and spatially targeting the fungal polyketide synthase ArmB to the vacuolar compartment, we enhanced orsellinic acid accumulation to 8.50 mg/L. items.title: Rewiring the Terpenoid Metabolic Network for Crop Improvement
items.summary: Terpenoids are the largest and most chemically diverse class of plant metabolites, and they span the full range from strictly essential primary metabolism to lineage-specific specialized chemistry. Because plant terpenoids derive from the same two five-carbon precursors, IPP and DMAPP, the network is unusually interconnected: a change made at one point is felt at others. Engineering a terpenoid trait in a crop therefore involves not only biosynthetic capacity but also rewiring, in which existing flux is redirected toward a different product, compartment, organ, or developmental window.
